chunks: Ḥafṣ ibn ʿUmar narrated from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said:
The Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم was asked, “What is the expiation for backbiting?” He said, “You seek forgiveness for the one whom you backbit, just as you mentioned him.”

key_terms.اغْتَبْتَهُ: you backbit him; you spoke of him negatively in his absence
key_terms.الِاغْتِيَابِ: backbiting; mentioning someone in their absence in a blameworthy way
key_terms.تَسْتَغْفِرُ: you seek forgiveness; you ask Allah for pardon
key_terms.ذَكَرْتَهُ: you mentioned him; you referred to him in speech
key_terms.كَفَّارَةُ: expiation; the act that atones for a wrongdoing

ai.seo_question: What is the expiation for backbiting in a hadith from the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم?
ai.summary: This hadith teaches that the expiation for backbiting is to seek forgiveness for the person who was backbitten. It emphasizes moral accountability for speech and directs the believer toward repentance and repairing harm through seeking divine pardon for the other person.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.4327 - Hafs ibn Umar narrated from Abu Abdillah (as) that the Messenger of Allah (swt) (peace be upon him and his family) was asked: "What is the expiation for backbiting?"
Imam (as) said: "You should seek forgiveness for the one you have backbitten, just as you mentioned him."
